chunks: And from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) that he said:
The believer is the brother of the believer like one single body, when a part of it is lost, the rest of the body becomes affected.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used to describe the relationship between believers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali (AS) in *Kitab al-Mumin*, this hadith employs the organic metaphor of a single body to define the spiritual and social cohesion of the *Ummah*, a concept central to Shia ethical teachings on communal responsibility. It underscores that the faith of an individual is inextricably linked to the collective well-being of the community, reflecting the principle of *Tawatur* in social conduct. This imagery reinforces the idea that neglecting one member’s plight is akin to a systemic failure of the entire religious body.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 85. It has been reported that Abu Ja'far or Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
Believers are brothers of one another, like one physical body from which when one part is lost, the whole body becomes affected.
